name: Wind-dried persimmon
summary: Persimmons hung and dried in the wind, a Da Lat specialty from the orchards on Mimosa Pass.
origin: Vietnam Tourism calls wind-dried persimmon a famous Da Lat specialty. A March 2025 Lam Dong science bulletin names hồng treo gió Đà Lạt among OCOP strengths.
texture: The provincial innovation center says the dried fruit stays very sweet, soft and chewy, and fragrant, after it is hung in controlled temperature, humidity, and wind.
taste: Vietnam Tourism says the fresh fruit that goes to the drying line is ripened until yellow. The innovation center’s taste line is the dried sweet chew, above.
howToEat: Buy it to take home, or see the drying at the orchards. Vietnam Tourism’s garden article puts the usual season in late October and November. Its September article says the crunchy season runs from September through December. Both are printed.
where: From the centre, Vietnam Tourism sends you along Trần Hưng Đạo, through Khe Sanh, to the end of Mimosa Pass, where the orchards sit on both sides. It names Lê Vân garden on Mimosa. A shop price in town is Check on arrival.
priceBand: Check on arrival. The innovation center says liên hệ and does not print a đồng figure.
